# mixparfmCWM

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of mixparfmCWM is to provide a flexible framework for fitting finite mixtures of parametric frailty models with random covariates. Possible baseline hazards: exponential, Weibull, inverse Weibull (Fréchet), Gompertz, lognormal, and loglogistic. Possible frailty distributions: gamma and inverse Gaussian (both with mean 1 and unknown variance), plus the no-frailty option.

Estimation maximizes the classification log-likelihood of the shared-frailty cluster-weighted model with an ICM-CEM algorithm (a classification EM algorithm whose classification step is carried out by iterated conditional modes): the classification step updates one label at a time while retaining the joint group-by-component shared-frailty contribution, and the M-step refits each component's parametric frailty model (warm-started, with a floor on the frailty variance). The component-wise likelihood routines are adapted from the [parfm](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=parfm) package (GPL-2), which is why mixparfmCWM is distributed under GPL-2; no other package beyond `mclust` and `survival` is required at runtime. Multiple random starts with best-objective selection are supported via `control_EM(n_start = ...)`.

This repository is associated with the paper *Cluster-weighted modeling of lifetime hierarchical data for profiling COVID-19 heart failure patients (2025+)* by Caldera, Cappozzo, Masci, Forlani, Antonelli, Leoni, Paganoni, Ieva. [https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.12230](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.12230)

## Installation

You can install the development version of mixparfmCWM from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("AndreaCappozzo/mixparfmCWM")
```

Note: from version 0.1.0 the package is self-contained and does not require the development version of [parfm](https://github.com/AndreaCappozzo/parfm); earlier versions required it.
